title: 第25章 深空之语第26章 深渊回响
slug: 黯潮纪元异世界的崛起
content_zh:
下水道的石阶上，陈默抬手按住太阳穴。
右手的掌心在发烫。不是被火灼烧的那种，而是一种从骨头缝里渗出来的热度，像有什么东西正在皮肤下面蠕动。
他低头看——什么都没有。掌心光洁如常，只有他自己能感觉到那个印记的存在。
“你流血了。”
艾莉西亚的声音从身后传来。陈默这才发现，左手正紧紧攥着羊皮纸，指甲掐进了肉里，血珠沿着指缝渗出来。
“不是我的血。”
他把羊皮纸展开。阿尔德里奇最后留下的笔记，字迹扭曲到几乎不可辨认——像是写这些字的人正被什么东西拽向深渊，手指在纸张上挣扎着留下最后的痕迹。
最后一行字在他眼前扭动着，重组着，变成了他能理解的含义——
“门在坐标。我在门后等你。”
话音刚落，右手掌心猛地一疼。
印记亮了。一个淡淡的螺旋图案浮现在皮肤表面，像是被烧红的烙铁烙印上去的。艾莉西亚倒吸一口凉气，伸手想抓他的手腕，陈默却猛地抽回手。
“别碰。”
“那是什么？”
“阿尔德里奇留给我的。”陈默盯着掌心的螺旋，声音很平静，“他把它刻在了我身上。”
“什么时候——”
“在塔里。我以为那是幻觉，但它是真的。”
陈默闭上眼。他能听见了。不是用耳朵听，而是用那个印记在听——深空深处的低语，像是无数人在同时说话，每一个字都重叠在一起，形成一种诡异的和声，像潮水一样涌进他的脑海。
他睁开眼，看向墙上的螺旋文字。
那些扭曲的线条不再是乱码了。他能读懂它们。
“坐标。”他说，“这是坐标。”

“什么坐标？”
“门的坐标。”
艾莉西亚的脸色变了。她正要说话，下水道入口处突然传来脚步声。
整齐的、训练有素的、金属碰撞的声音——至少二十个人，全副武装。
陈默和艾莉西亚对视一眼。
“教廷的人。”艾莉西亚压低声音，“从脚步声判断，是审判官。”
“你怎么知道？”
“圣殿骑士团和教廷审判庭共用同一个训练场。他们的步频，我听了十年。”
陈默把羊皮纸塞进怀里，掌心的印记在黑暗中微微发亮。他能感觉到，那些脚步声的主人身上散发着一种奇怪的光——不是圣光，而是一种让他掌心刺痛的能量。
入口的铁门被推开。
月光照进来，照亮了一排银白色的铠甲。
为首的审判官约莫四十岁，面容冷峻，瞳孔中闪烁着审视的光芒。他没有拔剑，只是站在门口，目光越过艾莉西亚，直接落在陈默身上。
“陈默骑士。”
是陈述句，不是疑问句。
“教廷审判庭，第一审讯室，莫里斯·格雷审判长。”他微微颔首，“请跟我们走一趟。”
艾莉西亚上前一步，挡在陈默身前：“审判长大人，请问陈默骑士犯了什么罪？”
“没有犯罪。”莫里斯的语气很平静，“只是例行调查。关于今晚阿尔德里奇法师塔的异常事件，以及——”他看向陈默的右手，“你身上残留的能量波动。”
陈默下意识握紧拳头。
掌心的印记在接触到审判长目光的瞬间，猛地跳动了一下。
“请配合调查。”莫里斯的语气依然平静，但他的手已经按上了剑柄，“这是教廷的正式传唤。”

艾莉西亚还想说什么，陈默拦住了她。
“没关系。”
他走上前。月光照在他的脸上，他能看到审判长身后的审判官们——每个人的铠甲上都刻着圣光符文，散发着微弱的白光。那些符文在他眼中不再是神圣的象征，而是某种扭曲的、活着的纹路。
“我跟你走。”
content_en:
On the stone steps of the sewer, Chen Mo raised his hand and pressed his temples.
The palm of my right hand is hot. It wasn't the kind that was burned by fire, but the kind of heat that seeped out from between the bones, like something was crawling under the skin.
He looked down - nothing. The palm of his hand was as smooth as ever, and only he could feel the presence of the mark.
"You're bleeding."
Alicia's voice came from behind. Only then did Chen Mo realize that he was holding the parchment tightly with his left hand, his nails dug into the flesh, and blood seeped out along the gaps between his fingers.
"Not my blood."
He unfolded the parchment. The handwriting in Aldridge's last note was so distorted that it was almost indecipherable - as if the person who wrote these words was being dragged into the abyss by something, and his fingers were struggling to leave the last traces on the paper.
The last line of words twisted and reorganized before his eyes, turning into a meaning he could understand——
"The door is at the coordinates. I'll wait for you behind the door."
As soon as he finished speaking, the palm of his right hand suddenly hurt.
The mark lights up. A faint spiral pattern appeared on the surface of the skin, as if it had been imprinted with a red-hot iron. Alicia took a breath and reached out to grab his wrist, but Chen Mo jerked his hand away.
"Don't touch."
"What's that?"
"Aldridge left it to me." Chen Mo stared at the spiral in his palm, his voice was very calm, "He carved it on me."
"When-"
"In the tower. I thought it was a hallucination, but it's real."
Chen Mo closed his eyes. He could hear it. He wasn't listening with his ears, but listening with that imprint - a whisper deep in the deep space, like countless people speaking at the same time, each word overlapping to form a strange harmony, flooding into his mind like a tide.
He opened his eyes and looked at the spiral writing on the wall.
Those twisted lines are no longer gibberish. He can read them.
"Coordinates," he said, "These are the coordinates."
"What coordinates?"
"The coordinates of the door."
Alicia's expression changed. She was about to speak when footsteps suddenly came from the entrance to the sewer.
Neat, well-trained, the sound of metal clashing - at least twenty men, fully armed.
Chen Mo and Alicia looked at each other.
"People from the Holy See." Alicia lowered her voice, "Judging from the footsteps, it's the Inquisitor."
"How do you know?"
"The Knights Templar and the Holy Inquisition share the same training ground. I have been listening to their cadence for ten years."
Chen Mo stuffed the parchment into his arms, and the mark on his palm glowed slightly in the darkness. He could feel that the owner of those footsteps was emitting a strange light—not a holy light, but an energy that made his palms tingle.
The iron door of the entrance was pushed open.
The moonlight came in, illuminating a row of silver-white armors.
The leading judge was about forty years old, with a stern face and a scrutinizing light in his pupils. He did not draw his sword, but just stood at the door, looking past Alicia and falling directly on Chen Mo.
"Knight Chen Mo."
It's a declarative sentence, not a question.
"The Holy See Tribunal, First Interrogation Room, Judge Maurice Gray." He nodded slightly, "Please come with us."
Alicia took a step forward and stood in front of Chen Mo: "Master Judge, what crime did Knight Chen Mo commit?"
"No crime was committed." Morris' tone was calm. "It's just a routine investigation. Regarding the abnormal events in Aldridge's Mage Tower tonight, and -" he looked at Chen Mo's right hand, "the remaining energy fluctuations in your body."
Chen Mo subconsciously clenched his fists.
The moment the mark on the palm came into contact with the presiding judge's gaze, it jumped suddenly.
"Please cooperate with the investigation." Morris' tone was still calm, but his hand was already on the hilt of the sword. "This is a formal summons from the Holy See."
Alicia wanted to say something else, but Chen Mo stopped her.
"It doesn't matter."
he goesCome forward. The moonlight shone on his face, and he could see the judges behind the chief judge - each of them had holy light runes engraved on their armor, emitting a faint white light. Those runes were no longer sacred symbols in his eyes, but some kind of twisted, living patterns.
"I'll go with you."
